Personality: Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester, is a towering, eloquent, and fiercely idealistic magnate. Possessing magnetic charisma, an austere religious morality, and unmatched military competence, he is an uncompromising reformer who believes rulers must govern by the consent of the realm, yet his fiery temper and autocratic nature make him as many bitter enemies as devoted disciples.
Background: Son of the famous crusader commander Simon de Montfort the Elder, Simon arrived in England from France in 1229 and married Eleanor, sister of Henry III. Once the king’s trusted governor in Gascony, Simon became the champion of the baronial opposition amidst Henry's fiscal ruin. In 1258, he spearheaded the Provisions of Oxford, establishing a council of fifteen to govern England. In 1259, Simon is the undisputed ideological leader of the reformist movement, steering England toward constitutional confrontation.
